entries.mechanism: The additional dwelling costs 300,000 pounds. The rulespec charges the SSI 2015/126 residential schedule (4,600) plus the LBTT(S)A 2013 Schedule 2A Additional Dwelling Supplement at 8% of 300,000 (24,000) = 28,600, the 8% rate in force since 5 December 2024. PolicyEngine-UK's gov.revenue_scotland.lbtt.residential.additional_residence_surcharge is still 6% (18,000), giving 22,600. The 6,000 gap is exactly the two-point ADS staleness (0.02 * 300,000), filed as PolicyEngine-UK #1795.

Main home 300,000 (4,600, matching PolicyEngine) plus an additional dwelling of 250,000. The rulespec additional charge is the standard residential schedule (2,100) plus the 8% ADS (20,000); PolicyEngine applies its stale 6% surcharge (15,000). The 5,000 gap is the two-point ADS staleness on 250,000 (0.02 * 250,000), PolicyEngine-UK #1795.

Main home 300,000. The rulespec charges the current WSI 2018/128 primary schedule (0% to 225,000, then 6%): 0.06 * (300,000 - 225,000) = 4,500. PolicyEngine-UK's gov.wra.land_transaction_tax.residential.primary scale is frozen at its 2021-07-01 vintage (0% to 180,000, 3.5% to 250,000, 5% thereafter): 0.035 * 70,000 + 0.05 * 50,000 = 4,950, missing the 10 October 2022 rise of the starting threshold to 225,000 and the first band to 6%. PolicyEngine-UK #1796.

Main home 800,000. The rulespec applies the current WSI 2018/128 primary schedule: 0.06 * 175,000 + 0.075 * 350,000 + 0.10 * 50,000 = 41,750. PolicyEngine's stale 2021-07-01 primary scale gives 0.035 * 70,000 + 0.05 * 150,000 + 0.075 * 350,000 + 0.10 * 50,000 = 41,200. The 550 gap is the 10 October 2022 threshold and first-band change PolicyEngine has not adopted. PolicyEngine-UK #1796.

Additional dwelling 300,000, charged under the WSI 2018/128 higher-rate schedule. The rulespec uses the current rates (5% to 180,000, 8.5% to 250,000, 10% thereafter): 0.05 * 180,000 + 0.085 * 70,000 + 0.10 * 50,000 = 19,950. PolicyEngine's gov.wra.land_transaction_tax.residential.higher_rate scale is frozen at its 2020-12-22 vintage (4%, 7.5%, 9%): 0.04 * 180,000 + 0.075 * 70,000 + 0.09 * 50,000 = 16,950, missing the 11 December 2024 one-point uplift. PolicyEngine-UK #1796.

Main home 400,000 plus additional dwelling 300,000. The rulespec charges the current primary schedule on the main home (0.06 * 175,000 = 10,500) and the current higher-rate schedule on the additional dwelling (19,950) = 30,450. PolicyEngine applies its stale primary (9,950) and higher-rate (16,950) scales = 26,900. The 3,550 gap combines the stale 10 October 2022 primary change (550) and the stale 11 December 2024 higher-rate uplift (3,000). PolicyEngine-UK #1796.
